paragraphs.source_en: Figure 5. 5 A sample of now-slices for a variety of observers (real or hypothetical) situated at a variety of distances from earth, moving with a variety of velocities. move freely, then reality encompasses all of the events in spacetime. The total loaf exists. Just as we envision all of space as really being out there, as really existing, we should also envision all of time as really being out there, as really existing, too. Past, present, and future certainly appear to be distinct entities. But, as Einstein once said, "For we convinced physicists, the distinction between past, present, and future is only an illusion, however persistent."5 The only thing that's real is the whole of spacetime. Experience and the Flow of Time In this way of thinking, events, regardless of when they happen from any particular perspective, just are. They all exist.
